[{"id": "nnvMTG5Sl5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🪙Finances Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "B-CtTCmVDX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The finances module contains features related to the finances of the church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fin_ws_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Finances workspace starts with the work that waits for you. Gifts with No Person lists the paid online gifts that no person is linked to. Donations Needing Review lists the online gifts whose charge does not agree with the gift. Pending Expenses lists the expenses that are saved but not submitted. Pending Alms Requests lists the alms requests that wait for a decision, and the approved requests that wait for their expense. Each list shows the oldest first. Under them, the graphs show weekly giving, giving by fund, expenses and the budget summary.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w8oEjl0tNc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "💵Collections", "col": 12}}, {"id": "z52PVRpfzT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A collection tracks donations from people for specific functions.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hh6-W_FmMh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each time a collection is taken, a New Collection should be created. When creating a new collection note the following:
- Link the collection to the Function where you took it. The Function list shows today's services first and then the past ones, latest first. When you choose a Function on a new collection, Churchit sets Date to the day and time of that service. Giving statements count each gift by this date, so keep it on the day the gifts were received, also when you enter the collection days later.
    - By regularly linking functions to collections, it will be possible later to run reports to see collection amounts for specific function types, etc.
- Remember: After saving a collection, it will be in a draft state. In order to finalize the collection, you will need to 'Submit' the collection. Once submitted, it cannot be modified unless you cancel and amend it. Do not cancel and amend the collection of an online gift: cancelling it marks the gift Refunded, and Churchit does not let you amend it.
    - See the 'Terminology' section in the Help guide for more information about document states (draft / submitted / cancelled / amended / etc).
- The form starts with Date, Function and the totals, and the Donations table comes next. Fund Totals and Payment Type Totals show under the table when it has donations. Notes is folded, and it opens by itself when it has text.
- In the Collection list, a draft shows Unbalanced (red) when its donations do not add up to the Expected Total, and Ready to Submit (orange) when they do. Each collection is titled with its Function and its date in full, for example Sunday Worship, Tuesday, October 20, 2026. An older title changes when the collection is saved again.
- After you save the collection, click View, then Bank Reconciliation Report, at the top right of the form. This report can be used to compare with bank deposit reports.
- Print (Ctrl+P) opens the Collection Count Sheet.
- To email a receipt to each giver when a collection is submitted, tick Email Receipts on the Messages tab of Giving Settings. Each giver who has an email address gets one email with their amount. Online gifts already send their own receipt. This setting is off by default. While it is off, a submitted collection shows a note that givers are not emailed a receipt, with a link to Giving Settings. Imported batches send none. The email uses the Email Template Donation Acknowledgment. If you made your own copy of the Donation Acknowledgment Notification, turn the copy off when you turn this setting on.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kVjzsXy2-5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open the Collections list from the Finances sidebar. The Collection Count Sheet print format shows the Cash, Check and Other amount of each fund, with the totals. The collection reports, such as Donations, Donations by Person and Bank Reconciliation, are in the Giving folder of the sidebar. The count sheet shows the name of the function. Under the fund table, it lists the non-cash gifts with the person, the fund and the description. Bank Reconciliation does not show non-cash gifts, because they do not go to the bank. In Bank Reconciliation you can select only a draft or a submitted collection. If you open it for a cancelled collection, a red message tells you that the collection is cancelled.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8K2QjgOLSb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🤲Donations", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bZ3I5EEmVO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A donation tracks the amount given from a person toward a church fund. For tracking monies given to people in need, see Alms below.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HSRUNh_Fan", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When adding donations to a collection, note the following:
- Each donation row has Person, Amount, Fund, Check # and Payment Type. Type a name or an envelope number in Person. Press Tab to go to the next column. Tab in Payment Type adds the next row. A new row starts with the fund and the payment type of the row above it. The first row starts with the Default Fund of Giving Settings. To see Notes, and the Description of a non-cash gift, open the row: they are under More, which opens by itself when the row has notes or a non-cash payment type.
- After entering each donation, the collection total and fund totals will be updated in real-time.
- If a single donation check specifies multiple funds, enter it as two separate donations (one for each fund).
- Additional payment types can be added if needed.
- When entering a donation from a specific person (i.e. Check donation or Cash Envelope), it is highly recommended to link the donation to the person.
   - By regularly linking donations to persons, end-of-year statements and individual person donation reports can be created.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "izAJqBHJ3P", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Fund messages. When you submit or cancel a collection, an expense or a fund transfer, a short message at the bottom right tells how much each fund changed. A fund whose donation rows add up to 0 gets no message. When money goes out of a fund and its balance goes below zero, a message tells the new balance. A gift into a fund that is below zero does not show this message. A person who gives online does not see these messages. Amounts show in the currency of your site (System Settings).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "finDateWarn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Dates. When you save a collection, an expense or a fund transfer with a date more than 30 days after today, or more than one year before today, an orange message asks you to check the date. If the year is wrong, correct it before you submit. Churchit still saves the date, so you can enter old records. A Data Import shows no message.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fin_r3_envelope", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Envelope numbers. A person can have an Envelope Number: the number on their offering envelopes or the reference on their bank gifts. When you enter a gift, type the envelope number in the Person field of the donation row to find the giver. Two people in one church cannot have the same number.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fin_r3_noncash", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Non-cash gifts. When someone gives property, such as equipment or goods, and not money, add a donation row with the Payment Type Non-Cash. Type a description of what was given in Description, under More in the row, and keep the amount 0. When you choose the Non-Cash payment type, Churchit sets the amount to 0 and opens the row, so you can type the description. Churchit does not let you save a non-cash row with an amount or without a description, because the church describes the gift and does not state its value. The giver's statement shows the description in place of an amount. Non-cash gifts do not change fund balances or collection totals. You can mark another Payment Type as Non-Cash on its form. The Payment Type list has a Non-Cash column.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Z1nAaK7FS7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The donation reports, such as Person Donations, YTD Giving by Person and First-Time Givers, are in the Giving folder of the Finances sidebar. YTD Giving by Person ends with a Total row, and its Avg Gift is the total amount divided by the total number of gifts.  Donations has From and To dates (this month at first) and filters for fund, payment type and person. It shows the newest gift first and ends with a total. Donations by Person also ends with a total. A gift of donated property (Non-Cash) does not count as a gift in YTD Giving by Person, First-Time Givers or Donations by Person, or in the Givers number of Weekly Metrics. In YTD Giving by Person, # Gifts counts a check one time, also when it is split across funds. The cash or other payments of one person in one collection count as one gift. Prior Year shows only gifts of money. In First-Time Givers, First Gift Amount is all the money that the person gave on the day of the first gift. Person Donations has From and To dates (this year at first). The Giving by Fund (This Year) chart on the Finances workspace shows the gifts of this year to the ten largest funds.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "finDates1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The donation and expense reports count only submitted collections and expenses. A report or a giving statement for a date range includes all of its last day, so a gift at 11:59 PM on the last day counts. The Expenses report has From and To dates (this month at first) and filters for expense type and fund. It ends with a total. If you select a group expense type, such as Utilities, the report also shows the types under it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "givingDates1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Giving on the Person form. A gift counts toward a person's First Gift, Last Gift and Lapsed Giver when its collection is submitted. A draft or cancelled collection does not count. Lapsed Giver is ticked when the last gift was more than 90 days ago but within the last year. The Lapsed Givers list, in the Giving folder of the Finances sidebar, shows these people with their first and last gift dates and when they last attended. A Church Manager can have it emailed to a finance user with ⋯ > Setup Auto Email. Only Church Finance, Church Manager and System Manager users see these fields.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "💳Online giving", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_setup", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members and guests give online on the Give page. Churchit uses the payment gateways of the Payments app, and it works with two of them: Stripe and PayPal. The Payments app is a separate Frappe app, and Churchit does not install it. Until a System Manager installs it, online giving, sign-up payments and form payments are off, Giving Settings shows a notice, and you cannot tick Enable Online Giving. Online payments in the Churchit README tells how to install it on Frappe Cloud, with Docker and on a bench. To set up online giving:
1. A System Manager installs the Payments app on the site.
2. A System Manager enters the account keys in Stripe Settings or PayPal Settings. Only a System Manager can see and change the gateway settings and keys.
3. Open Giving Settings. On the Online Giving tab, add the gateway in Payment Gateways, mark one row as the default, and tick Enable Online Giving. On a new site this box is not ticked.
4. On each fund that people can give to, tick Allow giving to this fund.
Without a gateway, the Give page shows that online giving is unavailable. The Give link shows in the website menu and footer only while online giving is on. The Give page itself still opens from a link and shows Other Ways to Give.
Gifts, prices and statements use the Currency in Giving Settings. When it is empty, they use the site currency. On a new site it is empty. A sign-up with a price then waits for a payment by hand, and a form with a price asks the person to contact the church office.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_limits", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Limits of the two gateways.
- Stripe cannot ask for 3-D Secure, the check in which the bank asks the card holder to confirm the payment. When a card needs 3-D Secure, the gift is declined. In the UK and in the EU many cards need it, so churches there use PayPal.
- PayPal Settings holds one PayPal account for the whole site, so every church that uses PayPal gets its gifts in that one account. Stripe can hold one account for each church: add one Stripe Settings record for each account.
- The payment page of each gateway shows the card fields in a frame inside a page of your site. Thus the PCI DSS 4.0 rules for scripts on payment pages apply to your site: keep a list of the scripts on these pages with the reason for each, and make sure that you find out when a script changes. Ask your payment processor what it needs from you.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "givChurchGate1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Online giving with more than one church. Each gateway row in Giving Settings has a Church. Name a church and that gateway serves only it, which is how each congregation's gifts reach its own account; leave it blank and every church can use it. A church with its own gateways uses only those. Wording Per Church, on the Messages tab of Giving Settings, does the same for the thank you message and the statement acknowledgment, so a branch's receipts carry its own words.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "givOnline1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Online gifts. Online giving works with Stripe and PayPal. Giving Settings refuses a gateway of another kind, and the Give page does not offer one. When the gateway confirms a payment, Churchit compares the amount and the currency that the gateway charged with the Online Donation:
- When they agree, Churchit records the gift in a Collection and sets the status to Paid.
- When they do not agree, Churchit records nothing and sets the status to Needs Review. The Church Finance users of the gift's church get an alert that gives the charged amount and the gift amount. Check the payment in the gateway before you do anything else.
- When the gateway charged a gift but the gift stays Pending, for example because the confirmation did not arrive, the Church Finance users of its church get an alert each day. Open the gift and click Record Charged Gift. Churchit checks the payment again and records the gift one time.
The Online Donation list shows each gift by the donor's name, with its status in color: Pending (orange), Paid (green), Needs Review and Failed (red), Cancelled (gray) and Refunded (purple). To find a gift from its payment record, type the reference in the Transaction Reference filter. On the gift, the Payment section holds the gateway, the currency and the reference. It opens by itself when the gift needs review or failed.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_fee_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Processing fees", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_fee", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A giver can add the processing fee to a gift, so that the church gets the full gift. Open Giving Settings. On the Online Giving tab, in the gateway row, tick Offer Fee Cover and type the card rate in Fee Percent and Fixed Fee, for example 2.9 and 0.30. Fee Percent must be less than 100, and neither field can be less than 0. The Give page then shows \"Cover the processing fee\" with the amount, worked out with the card rate. Churchit calculates the fee on the server from these two fields, so the giver cannot change it. The fee is part of the gift: the Online Donation shows it in Covered Fee, and the collection, the receipt and the giving statement show the full payment.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_link_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Give links and QR codes", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_link", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open a fund that has Allow giving to this fund ticked and click Give Link. The dialog shows a QR code and the address of the Give page with this fund chosen.
- Click Download QR Code to get the code as an SVG file for a bulletin, a poster or a giving card.
- Click Copy Link to copy the address.
- To fill in an amount, add &amount=25 to the end of the address.
- To make a tap to give tag, write the address on an NFC tag with a phone app.
With more than one church, the address names the fund's church, and that church must be published.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_text_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Text-to-give", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_text", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With text-to-give, a person sends a text to a phone number and gets back a link to the Give page. Churchit does not receive texts, so your text provider sends this reply. Churchit does not log these texts, and they are not on any timeline. To set it up:
1. Get a separate phone number for giving from your text provider, for example Twilio. Do not use the number that sends your Church Emails and other texts, because the reply goes to every text that comes in.
2. Get the link. For the Give page, the link is your site address followed by /give, for example https://yourchurch.org/give. For one fund, click Give Link on the fund, then click Copy Link. This link looks like https://yourchurch.org/give?fund=FUND-0001. To fill in an amount, add &amount=25. With more than one church, the link also names the church, for example https://yourchurch.org/give?church=CHR-02&fund=FUND-0001.
3. Set the number to reply with the link to every text. A provider that has keyword replies can reply only to the texts that have the word GIVE. In Twilio, add a TwiML Bin with this text, and put your link in it: <Response><Message>Thank you for giving. Give here: https://yourchurch.org/give</Message></Response>. In the bin, write each & in the link as &, for example https://yourchurch.org/give?church=CHR-02&fund=FUND-0001. If you do not, Twilio does not accept the bin. Then open the phone number in Twilio. Under A message comes in, choose TwiML Bin and this bin, and save.
4. Send a text to the number from your own phone. Make sure that the link comes back and opens the Give page.
The text provider handles STOP replies to the giving number, as for all texts. The Communications manual tells how, in Text replies and STOP.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_other_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Other ways to give", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_other", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open Giving Settings and, on the Messages tab, write your bank transfer, standing order or mailing details in Other Ways to Give. The Give page shows this text below the form. When online giving is off, the page shows this text first, then a note that online giving is not available, with a link to the Contact page. A church can have its own text: add a row for it in Wording Per Church and fill in Other Ways to Give. A church with no text of its own shows the site text.
A signed-in member who has an envelope number sees it on the Give page as the payment reference to use. Enter these gifts in a collection, and type the envelope number in the Person field of the donation row to find the giver.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_guest_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Give a guest gift to a person", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_guest", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A guest who gives without logging in has no person on the gift, so the gift is not on a giving statement. To find these gifts, click Gifts with No Person at the top of the Finances workspace, or in the Giving folder of the Finances sidebar. The oldest gift is first. Open the Online Donation, set Person and save. The donation row of the gift's collection then names that person, with the person's email, and a comment on the collection says which gift changed. The next giving statement for that year includes the gift. Only Church Finance and Church Manager users can do this.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_refund_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Record a refund", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_refund", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Refund the gift at the payment processor first. Churchit does not send the refund.
- For a full refund in the same year as the gift, open the gift's collection and cancel it. Churchit removes the gift from the fund balance and sets the Online Donation to Refunded. If the gateway confirms the payment again later, Churchit records nothing. You cannot amend the cancelled collection.
- If you already exported the dates of the gift to your accounting system, do not cancel the collection. Make a new collection with a negative donation row for the full amount, as for a partial refund. Thus the GL Journal shows the refund.
- For a partial refund, or a refund in a later year, make a new collection with the date of the refund. Add a donation row for the same person and fund with a negative amount, for example -20, and submit it. The giving statement for the year of the refund shows the lower total.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "reg_pay_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Event registrations and paid forms. A function sign-up or a form with a price takes an online payment through the gateways of the Give page. The Ministries manual tells how to set the prices. Each payment comes in as a submitted Collection with one row for the fund of the function or the Question Set, and no person, so it is not on a giving statement. It goes to the church of the function or the set, or to the church that shared it. When the gateway charged an amount that is not the amount due, or charged a record that is already paid, Churchit records nothing and alerts the Church Finance users of that church. Each day, Churchit also alerts them about sign-ups and form responses that a gateway charged but that are not recorded.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "reg_refund_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Registration payments by hand. For a sign-up paid in cash or by check, open the sign-up and click Payment, then Record Offline Payment. Churchit adds no Collection, so put the money in the weekly collection. When a payment arrives after a sign-up lost its seats, or when a paid sign-up is cancelled or declined, its Payment Status is Refund Due and Church Finance gets an alert. Refund it at the payment processor and cancel its Collection or add a negative donation row, as for a gift. Then click Payment, then Record Refund on the sign-up, or Record Refund on the Form Response. Only Church Finance and Church Manager users can do this.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "stm_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🧾Giving statements", "col": 12}}, {"id": "stm_make", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A giving statement lists a giver's gifts for a period, for the giver's tax records. In the Giving Statement list, click Generate Statements and enter From Date and To Date. Churchit makes or rebuilds the statements from the submitted collections in those dates.
- A household gets one statement. If the primary contact of the household changes, run Generate Statements again: the household keeps its statement, and it goes to the new contact.
- Generate Statements removes only statements that an earlier run made, for people whose gifts it no longer covers. It never removes a statement that you made by hand, a statement that was emailed, or a statement of another church. Statements made before this release stay until you delete them. After you change Group Statements By, delete the old statements of that kind by hand.
- When no gift in those dates has a named giver, Generate Statements says so and makes no statement.
- A statement shows only gifts to funds that have Tax Deductible ticked (see Funds below).
- A non-cash gift shows its description in place of an amount, and the total counts only money.
The list shows each statement as Emailed (green), Not Sent (orange) or No Email (red). Print opens the Contribution Statement. For a household, it shows the household name and the mailing address of the household. If the household has none, it shows the address of the person it is addressed to.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "stm_email_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Email the statements", "col": 12}}, {"id": "stm_email", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In the Giving Statement list, click Email Statements. Enter the same From Date and To Date that you used to generate the statements, then click Email. Churchit sends each statement to the giver's primary email at the time it sends, with the statement attached as a PDF. The emails go out in the background, so you can continue to work. Email Statements tells you how many will be emailed, how many have no email address and how many were already emailed. If the site cannot send email yet, ask a System Manager. You can still print the statements from the list.
- A statement with no email address is not sent. Print it and mail it instead.
- A giver who unsubscribed from all email gets no statement email, and the statement is not marked as emailed.
- A statement that was emailed once is not sent again. If you generate the statements again and a gift on a statement changes, the next Email Statements sends the new statement. To send all of them again, tick \"Send again to statements already emailed\".
- Each email is written in the Access Log. To change the text of the email, edit the Email Template \"Giving Statement\".", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Pb91OTOhF1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Giving statements with more than one church. A statement is issued in your church, also for a giver from another church who gave at your collections. A giver who gave at two churches gets a statement from each. You cannot move a statement to a church that is not yours, or take one from another church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gimp_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📥Import giving history", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gimp_intro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "You can add past gifts from another church system, from a spreadsheet or from your payment processor. Churchit uses Frappe's Data Import tool. Data Import reads the file, shows a preview, and adds the gifts in the background. Church Finance users, Church Managers and System Managers can import gifts.
Each row of the file is one gift. Churchit adds each gift as a donation to a draft collection. The gifts of one batch on one date go in one collection, and its Expected Total is the sum of these gifts. Check each draft collection and submit it. The gifts count in the funds, the reports and the giving statements only after you submit the collection. Churchit does not send a thank you email for an imported collection.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gimp_columns", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The file has these columns. You must fill in Gift ID, Date, Amount, Fund and Payment Type.
- 'Gift ID': the ID of the gift in the system it comes from, for example a Stripe charge ID. Churchit imports each gift one time.
- 'Date' and 'Amount': the date of the gift and the full amount that the giver paid.
- 'Fund' and 'Payment Type': a fund and a payment type of your church. A gift with the payment type Check also needs a 'Check Number'.
- 'Imported From' and 'Person ID': the system name and the ID of the giver from your People import. Leave 'Imported From' blank when you imported the people from a spreadsheet.
- 'Email': finds the giver when the Person ID does not. Only one person in your churches can have this email.
- 'Batch': the gifts of one batch and one date go in one collection. When you leave it blank, the batch is the name of the Data Import.
- 'Notes': text for the donation.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gimp_steps", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. In the Finances sidebar, open Setup and click Data Imports, then click Add Data Import. Set Document Type to Giving Import. Keep Import Type as Insert New Records.
2. Save, and click Download Template to get the columns. You can also use the export of your payment processor (see below).
3. Upload the file and click Next. When the file has a column name that Churchit does not know, select the Churchit column that it agrees with, or do not import the column.
4. Look at the preview. A row that cannot be imported stops the import. Correct the file, or click Skip Row.
5. Click Import. Then open the Collection list, filter on Import Batch, check each draft collection and submit it.
If your church uses its own copy of the Donation Acknowledgment notification, set its Condition to doc.donations and not doc.import_batch before you submit imported collections. If you do not, each giver gets an email for each old gift.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gimp_refusals", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The preview stops a row when:
- Churchit does not know its fund or payment type, or its fund belongs to another church.
- No person, or more than one person, has its Person ID or email.
- A donation already has its Gift ID. Thus a second import of the same file adds nothing. You can import the gift of a cancelled collection again.
- An earlier row of the file has the same Gift ID.
- Its payment type is a non-cash type, such as Non-Cash. Enter a non-cash gift in a collection with a description.
- An online donation that your payment processor charged has the same amount, date and email. This includes a Pending or Needs Review gift. Record that gift from the online donation, not from the import.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gimp_stripe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Import gifts from Stripe. Use this for gifts that givers make on the pages of Stripe, for example recurring gifts and bank debits. Churchit records the gifts from your Give page itself, so do not import them again.
1. In the Stripe Dashboard, open Payments, set the dates and click Export. Download the CSV file.
2. Open the file in a spreadsheet. Delete each row whose Description starts with \"Online gift to the\". These are the gifts from your Give page, which Churchit has already.
3. Delete each row whose Status is not Paid, and each row with an Amount Refunded.
4. Rename these columns: id to Gift ID, Created date (UTC) to Date, Customer Email to Email. Keep Amount. Delete the other columns.
5. Add the columns Fund and Payment Type, and fill in a fund and a payment type of your church on each row. You can add a Batch column, for example with the month.
6. Import the file with the steps above.
Stripe gives the date in UTC. A gift late in the evening can have the date of the next day.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "vVJ7g0tHHy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📊Funds", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4znr2XFUMc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Funds are used by churches to tag monies for a specific purpose. Some default funds are included (i.e. General, Building, Missions, etc), but additional funds can be created for your own purposes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "37szS6a0yE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When adding/managing a fund, note the following:
- The fund form has three tabs. Details has the name, the Balance, Allow giving to this fund and Tax Deductible. The Fundraising Goal section has Goal Amount, Goal Progress, Start Date and End Date. It opens by itself when the fund has a goal or a date. Ledger lists each transaction of the fund: the gifts of collections, the expenses and the fund transfers. Connections shows the records that use the fund in two groups, Giving (collections, online donations and pledge campaigns) and Spending (expenses and expense types).
- Churchit calculates the Balance from the transactions, so you cannot type it.

If your church also uses an accounting system, you can send it a journal of the gifts, expenses and fund transfers.
1. Open GL Account Mappings and add one mapping for each record. Mapping For tells what the record is. Record is the fund, payment type, expense type or church. Account is the account number or name exactly as your accounting system shows it.
2. Map each fund to the account its money goes to. Map each payment type (Cash, Check, Card) to the account the money comes into. Map each expense type to its expense account. Map your church to the account that pays expenses.
3. Open the GL Journal report and set From Date and To Date. Each submitted collection, expense and fund transfer in those dates gives lines whose debits equal its credits. The Memo names the source document. It never names a giver.
4. If a record has no mapping, the report shows one message that lists every record to map. Add the mappings and run the report again.
5. Use the report menu to export the journal as CSV, and import the file into your accounting system.
The journal shows only submitted documents. If you cancel a collection, expense or fund transfer after you export its dates, the journal does not show a reverse line. For a refund after an export, use a negative donation row (see Record a refund).
